title: Lesson 43 - Calling Agent API from an External System: Sessions, Identity, and When It Is the Right Seam
description: Given a scenario, identify when it's appropriate to use Agent API.

questions.question: An external service wants to call the agent and immediately use a structured value the agent's action produced, without dealing with a chat UI. Which shape fits?
options: Agent API in a single-turn synchronous call, reading the structured output variables from the response
A prompt template in Prompt Builder
A public Service agent with no integration
questions.explanation: The caller wants a programmatic request-response with structured output, which is exactly the synchronous Agent API pattern, not a chat surface.

questions.question: A chat widget holds a multi turn conversation with a customer and the agent must remember earlier questions. What should the integration do?
options: Create a new session for every message
Pass every earlier message again in each call
Create the session once and reuse the session id across turns so the agent retains context
questions.explanation: Multi-turn continuity comes from creating the session once and reusing its id, so the agent keeps the conversational context without the caller re supplying it.

questions.question: An integration must carry a specific customer's identity through to Salesforce so their own access governs the agent. Which approach fits?
options: Expose the client credential token in the browser
A shared integration user for everyone
A wrapper that strips identity for speed
An OAuth 2.0 token exchange flow that presents the user's identity provider token and maps it to a Salesforce user
questions.explanation: Token exchange carries the person's identity across the hop and maps it to a Salesforce user, instead of collapsing every caller into one shared service account.
